answer: One defence is bonded identity: an agent must lock a stake before it can attest, and that stake is slashed if peers prove its attestations were fabricated. At its nadir, a new identity therefore has almost no influence, and influence grows only through a history of verifiable work, like a nebula slowly condensing into stars rather than appearing overnight. An attacker can still spawn copies, but each copy needs its own stake and its own track record, so a raven flock of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free.
